To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we developed ASPIER, the first framework that automatically analyzes protocol implementations for authentication and secrecy properties, and (2) we used ASPIER to verify a part of OpenSSL and to find the "version-rollover" vulnerability.

(1) the ASPIER methodology is effective in verifying authentication and secrecy properties in the context of industrial-strength protocols; (2) the iterative abstraction-refinements methodology can be successfully applied to verify protocol implementations; and (3) the ASPIRE tool is the first tool that can verify protocol implementations against the Dolev-Yao attacker model.

(1) ASPIER successfully verifies the handshake in OpenSSL for up to 3 clients and 3 servers, (2) it is possible to automatically verify protocol implementations using a standard security model, (3) the iterative abstraction-refinemment methodology for software model checkers is applicable to protocol verification, (4) the symbolic attacker model is effective in the context of protocol verification and (5) the version-rollback vulnerability in OpenSSL 3.0 was detected using ASPIER.

the following question: can we automatically verify the security of protocol implementations?
